# dsh-task-dispatch
Deliver a message to a real DSH session **by session id**, and optionally wait for its reply.
It removes the human copy-paste relay between two agents: Codex, a script, or CI only needs HTTP to
hand a task to a running DSH session and read the answer back.
**Zero dependencies.** It declares no `@deepseek-ai/*` or third-party packages — only Node built-ins
plus the host's existing `sessionController` / `agents` / `sessions` services.
## Why not the existing bridge
`hermes-dsh-bridge` is broader, but as of 0.11.4 every `@deepseek-ai/*` dependency is pinned to `^0.
1.2-rc.1`. On DSH 0.2.x that installs a second copy of the same packages, the host loads the wrong v
ersion (observed: boot failure that also reset the profile's patch layer), and the plugin never runs
rsion (observed: boot failure that also reset the profile's patch layer), and the plugin never runs.
This plugin deliberately declares no host packages, so that class of conflict cannot happen. The tra
de-off: it only sends and waits — no file tools, approval bridge, or preset management.

## Configuration
| Field | Default | Meaning |

| `host` | `127.0.0.1` | Loopback only; any other value fails activation |
| `port` | `7391` | Liste

n port |
| `token` | none | When set, requests need `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |
## API
| Method | Path | Purpose |

| `GET` | `/health` | Liveness probe, no token |
| `GET` | `/sessions` | List **live** sessions (id

/ cwd / title / running) |
| `POST` | `/send` | Deliver a message, return immediately (202) |
| `POS
T` | `/ask` | Deliver, wait for the turn, return assistant text |
### `POST /send`
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- `sessionId` required; cold sessions are resumed automatically
- `mode` optional, `steer` interrupt

s instead of queueing
- Returns `{ ok, sessionId, requestId, afterSeq }`
### `POST /ask`
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- Same as `/send` plus waiting; returns `{ ok, reason, text, truncated }`
- `reason`: `idle` / `inpu

t-required` / `timeout`
- `text` is extracted from this turn's `assistant/message` events
- `timeout
Ms` defaults to 120000
## Use from Codex

Wrap that curl in an MCP server if you want Codex to call it as a tool.
## Security

- Listens on `127.0.0.1` only; non-loopback hosts are rejected in code
- Any local process can call

it, so set `token` before exposing anything
- It drives a real agent, which can execute commands and
edit files — treat it as local shell-level access
## Callback: not supported yet
The task result is **not pushed back** to the caller. There is no MCP server→client notification imp
lementation, and whether such a notification could wake an idle Codex session is unverified.
`notify` is a delivery *ledger*, not proof of receipt: `unsupported` / `pending` / `sending` / `sent
` / `failed`. A webhook returning 200 only means the HTTP endpoint answered.
Retrieve results by querying: `GET /tasks/:id` (`dsh_result`) or `POST /wait` (`dsh_wait`). Neither
by querying: `GET /tasks/:id` (`dsh_result`) or `POST /wait` (`dsh_wait`). Neither resends the task.
## Limitations

- `/sessions` lists live sessions only; a cold session still accepts `/send` if you know its id
- `/

ask` waits for one turn; for long work use `/send` plus polling, or raise `timeoutMs`
- No streaming
; only the turn's final text is returned
